description.narrative:
The World Food Programme (WFP) har ansökt om finansiering från Sida om 165 MSEK för att genomföra det treåriga projektet "Safety Net Activities" i Sudan under perioden 2019-2022. Sida har beslutat att stödja de två första åren med 133 miljoner SEK. Ett eventuellt stöd till ett tredje år är avhängigt utfallet av den utvärdering som ska genoföras under projektets andra år.
Insatsen syftar till att 1) Erbjuda inkomstgenererande aktiviteter och tekniskt stöd inom ramen för sociala trygghetssystem för att stödja hushåll med bristande livsmedelsförsörjning att reducera cykliska risker och hantera konsekvenser av klimatförändringar 2) Ge kapacitetsutvecklande stöd till jordbrukare och institutioner på lokal, delstats- och nationell nivå 3) Tillhandahålla flygförbindelser till aktörer inom humanitärt och långsiktigt utvecklingssamarbete.
Insatsen bidrar till WFP:s strategiska plan för Sudan 2019-2023. Förutom bidraget till WFP avsätts 200 000 SEK för förstärkt uppföljning samt metodutveckling.

The World Food Programme (WFP) has applied to Sida for funding of 165 MSEK to carry out the three year project "Safety Net Activities" in Sudan during the period 2019-2022. Sida has decided to fund the first two years of the project with 133 milion SEK. Possible support to a third year will depend on the outcome to the evaluation to be carried out during the second year of the project.
The intervention aims at 1) Offering asset-creation activities and technical assistance through safety nets to help food-insecure households to reduce risk and adapt to cliamte change 2) Provide capacity-strengthening support for farmers and local, state and national agricultural institutions 3) Air services are provided for the humanitarian and development community.
The intervention has a budget of 165 MSEK and is contributing to WFP's Country Stategic Plan 2019-2023. In addition to the contribution to WFP, 200 000 SEK is set aside for increased monitoring as well as methods development.

The intervention would mainly contribute to fulfilling Strategic Outcome no 3 (SO3) of WFP's Country Strategic Plan: food insecure people in targeted areas and food systems have increased resilience to shocks by 2024.
This would be achieved by the following broad activities, which each included a number of different outputs:
- Offer asset creation activities and technical assistance through safety nets to help food insecure households to reduce risk and adapt to climate change.
- Provide capacity strengthening support to farmers and local, state and national agricultural institutions.
- Improved access to logistics and transports for humanitarian and development actors to travel across Sudan.

sector.narrative: Food security policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The programme was implemented in an increasingly challenging and changing context. Firstly, the COVID-19 pandemic broke out in early 2020, as the project was rolled out. In October 2022, the military took over as the de facto government, and is still the de facto regime of Sudan. On April 15 2023, war broke out, which further disrupted programme activities and called for new adaptions of the programme.
Despite the many challenges WFP managed to achieve results that included;
The Productive Safety Nets (PSN) project was designed to boost resilience against shocks and foster long-term stability through collaboration with partners to integrate actions that tackle the root causes of vulnerability. By offering unrestricted cash, the PSN programme empowers individuals with the autonomy and resources to prioritise their own needs, thereby promoting self reliance within the targeted communities.
Before April 15 2023, the PSN programme was active in three localities within Kassala, four in North Kordofan, two in West Kordofan, and three in White Nile states. However, the outbreak of conflict led to WFP suspending ongoing development programmes after consultations with Sida and other development donors. Subsequently, WFP reassessed the PSN activities, determining that North and West Kordofan were no longer viable locations for the project due to the conflict's impact on security and access. WFP relocated PSN activities to more suitable areas of eastern Sudan. This decision was based on comprehensive risk assessment and consultations with local stakeholders to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the interventions.
In September 2023, WFPs management approved the resumption plan for the PSN project in the more secure regions of Sudan: Kassala, Gedarif, and White Nile. After thorough preparations, the project recommenced in November 2023. The preparations included capacity building workshops for local staff and partners, ensuring that all stakeholders were well equipped to implement the programme effectively. Since then, WFP reached 14 835 beneficiaries in Kassala state, bringing the total number of farmers reached by the PSN programme over the programme duration, January 2020 until April 2024, up to 252 115 farmers.
The Postharvest losses (PHL) project significantly affected the food security of smallholder farmers in Sudan. This project set out to improve grain handling and storage and support farmers through the provision of hermetic bags and postharvest training with a focus on boosting grain quality and safety through this project. In line with the overall ambition of improving the food security and livelihoods of smallholder farmers, the project was designed to increase household food availability by reducing pre and postfarm gate losses increasing household income by empowering smallholders to sell surplus grain and increasing food safety, health, and nutrition through the reduction of aflatoxin contamination, and other mycotoxins.
Through this project, these objectives were pursued via two components; soft components: training and other capacity building related activities, and, hard components: the distribution of hermetic bags and manuals, and the construction of community warehouses.
Prior to April 2023, PHL was active in North, West, and South Kordofan, as well as White Nile. After conflict broke out, the security situation and access to Greater Kordofan deteriorated significantly, leading to WFPs suspension of PHL in these three states. The project, however, was continued in White Nile. During the 2023-2024 season, the project was shifted to new states which were more conducive environments for PHL implementation. In consultation with Sida, Kassala, Gedarif, and Yabus in Blue Nile were selected. Implementation was also continued in Kauda, South Kordofan as per the plan.
From November 2023 to April 2024, WFP was able to reach 49 526 farmers across Kassala, Gedarif, White Nile, South Kordofan (Kauda) and Blue Nile (Yabus), exceeding the target of 32 600, bringing the total number of farmers reached by the PHL programme over the programme duration, since January 2020 until May 2024, to 68 510 farmers.
WFP provided reliable common services and expertise, including coordinating logistics, air transport, and telecommunications services, to humanitarian and development partners in Sudan. Flooding and conflict impeded access, particularly to areas with the greatest needs. Despite intensive efforts by the WFP, access remained a challenge throughout the contribution period.
Nevertheless, the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS) enabled a timely humanitarian response for 80 distinct user organizations. During 2024 UNHAS transported 8,063 passengers and 31 mt of cargo through 507 flights. The Logistics Cluster supported 90 organizations through coordination, information management, and access to common services, such as storage and road transport on an ad-hoc basis, to fill identified gaps. The Emergency Telecommunications Cluster expanded data connectivity to additional locations in 2024 reaching 70 sites and more than 40 humanitarian organizations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
